evidence: The proposed schedule is possible, but the demonstration does not reach a violation of the settled contract. Root Goal conditions the warning on receipt/acceptance being 'unconfirmed'; Message deadline contract makes expired pending rows due on the 'normal bounded scan', preserves terminal states, and says 'Late ACK clears the existing warning through normal lifecycle'. Invitation contract expressly says 'Only explicit recipient acceptance settles it automatically'; the invitation subtree likewise says timed invitations 'settle at acceptance'. Thus, at t0 an obligation is created with deadline D; at D it remains pending; at D+epsilon a genuine ACK/explicit acceptance settles it; at the next bounded scan it is already confirmed. Silent settlement does not reset D, invent confirmation, omit a still-pending overdue obligation, or lose an existing warning. Conversely, opening then passively clearing a warning also implements the specified lifecycle. The finding's final step needs an additional requirement that every historical deadline crossing produce a durable missed-deadline record even when genuine confirmation precedes observation. Neither the root acceptance clauses nor the receipt/invitation subtrees state that audit guarantee. The spec's 'Expiry notifies' and warning wording describe overdue notification, not an atomic historical-event ledger independent of settlement. A boundary test could document an implementation choice, but its absence does not establish a material gap against the stated bounded pending-confirmation contract.
